chunks: As for what Saʿd ibn ʿAbd Allah narrated from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad ibn ʿĪsā, from al-Ḥusayn ibn Saʿīd, from Ḥarīz ibn ʿAbd Allah, from Abū ʿAbd Allah عليه السلام, he said:

The overpowered sick person and the one who is unconscious may have the stoning done on his behalf and the tawaf performed on his behalf. So this does not contradict the reports we presented earlier, because the proper way regarding it is that we understand it to apply to one who cannot maintain his taharah and from whom ritual invalidation is not secure, such as one afflicted with abdominal illness and those similar to him. This indicates that.

key_terms.الْمَبْطُونِ: one afflicted with a stomach or bowel condition
key_terms.الْمَغْلُوبُ: one overcome by illness or incapacity
key_terms.يُرْمَى عَنْهُ: the stoning is performed on his behalf
key_terms.يُطَافُ عَنْهُ: the tawaf is performed on his behalf

ai.seo_question: Can tawaf and stoning be performed on behalf of a sick or unconscious person in hajj?
ai.summary: This passage gives a legal ruling concerning a sick or unconscious person during hajj rites, stating that certain acts may be performed on his behalf. It reconciles this with earlier reports by restricting the ruling to someone unable to maintain taharah or prone to hadath, such as a person suffering from abdominal illness.
